content.question: How does DBSCAN form a cluster, and when does it stop?
options: It assigns all points to the nearest centroid and stops when the centroids stop moving.
It starts from a randomly selected point and expands the cluster by recursively adding neighbouring points, stopping when all points are assigned to a cluster or labeled as noise.
It merges the closest clusters one by one and stops when the dendrogram is complete.
It stops as soon as the first core point is found, leaving all remaining points as noise.
content.answer: It starts from a randomly selected point and expands the cluster by recursively adding neighbouring points, stopping when all points are assigned to a cluster or labeled as noise.
